The method was applied to in situ Re–Os dating of various molybdenite samples ranging in age from 2.7 Ga to 23 Ma. The obtained ages are consistent with those determined by conventional bulk-sample analyses. The results demonstrate that for molybdenite older than 1.5 Ga, reliable in situ Re–Os ages consistent with bulk analyses can be obtained even when Re concentrations are as low as 2–5 ppm. In contrast, younger Mesozoic-Cenozoic molybdenite generally requires significantly higher Re contents (typically >100 ppm) to yield robust age determinations. Laser ablation in situ Re–Os dating of molybdenite provides an effective tool for investigating fine-scale geological processes in metal sulfide deposits and offers important constraints on the timing and genesis of mineralization.

title: The seven mysteries of Callisto: A science case for a next-generation orbiter and lander mission
abstract: Callisto, the outermost and least evolved Galilean moon, is a primordial witness to the Jupiter System’s formation that has recorded its evolution and exhibits dynamic present-day processes. In this article, we identify seven key mysteries that Callisto can illuminate: (1) the accretionary origin of the Galilean moons; (2) the early outer Solar System impact record; (3) the nature and maintenance of Callisto’s putative subsurface ocean; (4) its tidal coupling mechanisms with Jupiter; (5) the billions of years of its surface chemical evolution; (6) the dynamics of its tenuous atmosphere-ionosphere system; and (7) its unique location and potential role as a probe of Jovian magnetospheric processes. While the JUICE and Europa Clipper missions, currently in the cruise phase, will provide critical flyby data, fully resolving these interconnected puzzles demands a dedicated mission. We detail a science traceability matrix for a mission combining a long-duration, low-altitude (200 km or less) orbiter for global geophysical and compositional mapping with a geophysics/geochemistry-focused lander. An orbiter will measure the gravity field (for moment of inertia), internal structure, tidal deformation, and global surface properties, and offer the best possible location for a magnetospheric observatory. A lander will enable such transformative investigations as very broad-band seismology, precise geodetic tracking, and direct surface chemistry measurements. This synergistic orbiter-lander architecture is the definitive path to decoding Callisto’s frozen record, answering fundamental questions about icy moon formation and degree of internal differentiation, internal oceans, and moon-magnetosphere interactions. It will ideally complement the on-going inventory of Galilean icy moons and set a new benchmark for a deeper understanding of satellite systems across the outer Solar System.

title: Achieving highly efficient olivine carbonation: The critical roles of grinding method and elevated CO2 partial pressure
abstract: Mineral carbonation, which transforms CO 2 into stable carbonates via reaction with Ca- and Mg-silicates, offers a permanent and secure carbon sequestration pathway. Olivine is a highly reactive feedstock, and its carbonation kinetics are known to depend on particle size, CO 2 partial pressure ( \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) ), temperature, and additives. However, two key gaps persist in the current understanding. First, the time-dependent influence of \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) throughout the carbonation process remains unclear. Furthermore, the effect of the grinding method (wet vs. dry) is frequently oversimplified as reducing particle size, neglecting its concurrent alteration of other physicochemical properties. This study systematically addresses these gaps by investigating the carbonation of fine-grained olivine under varied \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) (5–14 MPa) at 185 °C. Reaction progress was tracked in real time using a flush-sampling batch reactor. Our results reveal that the wet-ground olivine, possessing a higher specific surface area (SSA), achieved significantly greater carbonation efficiency compared to the dry-ground sample. Kinetic analysis based on the shrinking core model (SCM) indicates that the formed porous carbonate layer does not act as a diffusion barrier but facilitates the reaction. Increasing \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) significantly enhanced the carbonation rate and final efficiency, with the maximum conversion reaching 98.45% at 14 MPa after 8 h. Furthermore, we identified that the reaction was most sensitive to \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) during the initial stage, with the most pronounced effect observed within the first hour. The primary mechanistic insight is that initial carbonation is predominantly controlled by \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) -driven dissolution, whereas at later stages, the available reactive surface area becomes the limiting factor. This work demonstrates that optimizing both the grinding method (preferring wet grinding for ex-situ applications) and employing elevated \({P_{{\rm CO}_2}}\) (⩾ 8 MPa for in-situ scenarios) are critical strategies for enhancing the efficiency and practical viability of olivine-based CO 2 sequestration.

title: Differentiation of intracontinental crustal magmas and its controlling mechanisms
abstract: The production and differentiation of felsic magmas are one of the key features of continental crust on Earth. Understanding the processes and mechanisms of highly differentiated magmas is crucial for unraveling lithospheric architecture and deep Earth processes, deciphering the evolution of transcrustal magmatic systems, and exploring the metallogenesis of critical metals. Granitic rocks widely occur in China, where their precursor magmas exhibit particularly pronounced differentiation. The highly differentiated granites are common in South China, the Himalaya, Xinjiang (Central Asia), and the Great Xing’an Range. They exhibit diverse characteristics, complex geological settings and significant mineralization potential, thus requiring further investigation. In this paper we present a review of recent progress in experimental petrology related to the formation of highly differentiated granites and outline their diagnostic mineralogical and geochemical indicators. We systematically analyze the spatiotemporal distribution, geochemical signatures, and formation mechanisms of highly differentiated granites in the above four regions. We suggest that such petrogenetic and metallogenic diversities are governed by multiple factors, including source compositions, tectonic setting, and heat and volatile supply. We identify some main challenges for the further study of highly differentiated intracontinental magmas: (1) experiments and simulations on key processes of crust-derived magmas; (2) clarifying spatiotemporal distribution patterns of highly differentiated granites; (3) understanding the physical mechanisms of crystal–melt separation; (4) constraining source nature and melting processes; and (5) constructing transcrustal magmatic system models. Addressing these issues may provide valuable insights into continental crust evolution and associated metallogenic diversity.

title: Six-year (2019–2024) persistent drought triggers large-scale tree mortality in the Helan Mountains
abstract: Over recent decades, the frequency and intensity of extreme heat and persistent drought events have increased, continuously intensifying climatic stress on forest ecosystems and contributing to more frequent tree mortality events. In 2023–2024, large-scale tree mortality occurred in the Helan Mountains, but its climatic driving mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we integrated automatic weather station observations from the mortality area, gridded climate data, remotely sensed vegetation indices, and large-scale atmospheric circulation data over the surrounding region to identify the main climatic drivers of this mortality event. The results show that during 2019–2024, monsoonal water vapor transport from the southeast was generally weak, mid-latitude low-level westerly moisture transport was either insufficient or displaced northward, and 500 hPa geopotential height showed persistent positive anomalies. Together, these atmospheric circulation anomalies weakened the effective moisture supply to the Helan Mountains, causing regional precipitation to remain significantly below the climatological mean. The persistent precipitation deficit kept soil moisture at low levels for an extended period and, combined with the increase in atmospheric evaporative demand induced by extreme heat, further intensified tree water stress, ultimately triggering large-scale tree mortality. Overall, long-term water deficit caused by persistent drought was the primary climatic driver of this large-scale tree mortality event in the Helan Mountains.

title: Research advances in surface water balance of the Asian Water Tower
abstract: The spatiotemporal distribution, variability, and underlying causes of the energy and water cycles on the Tibetan Plateau (TP) constitute one of the most fundamental and most important scientific questions in plateau research. Conventional studies have relied primarily on reanalysis data and meteorological station observations, both subject to notable uncertainties. Through the synergistic integration of remote sensing observations and models, scientific understanding of the principles governing the spatiotemporal distribution, variability, and causes of the TP energy and water cycle system has been substantially advanced. This paper systematically summarizes the progress achieved in model improvement and attribution analysis, including: the construction of high-resolution atmosphere-land surface models and multi-sphere hydrological simulation and assimilation systems that effectively reduced the wet bias of reanalysis data over the TP; the production of high-resolution atmospheric reanalysis data, near-surface meteorological forcing data, high spatiotemporal resolution water resource data, and other datasets, all of which have been released through the National Tibetan Plateau Data Center and have supported research on Asian Water Tower dynamics; and the elucidation that the dominant factor driving the warming and wetting of the TP is increased water vapor input from outside the plateau, driven by the interplay of the westerlies and monsoons, with a precipitation increase rate of 0.94 mm a −1 and a warming rate of 0.03 K a −1 .

title: Substorm-driven strong precipitation of low-energy radiation belt electrons: FY-3E observations
abstract: Using high-precision, pitch-angle-resolved measurements of tens to hundreds of keV electrons from the Fengyun-3E (FY-3E) satellite, we compare the dynamic response of the electron radiation belts to two contrasting geomagnetic events: an extreme superstorm in May 2024 and a moderate storm in January 2022. During the recovery phase of both storms, tens to hundreds of keV electron fluxes increased significantly and persisted for several to more than ten days, with electrons penetrating to much lower L-shells ( L ∼2) in the superstorm. Unlike these storm-associated electrons, a distinct population of electrons below ∼100 keV exhibited strong and transient enhancements independent of storm intensity and phase. These enhancements are related to substorm activity, which drives intense net precipitation (up to ∼10 5 cm −2 s −1 sr −1 keV −1 ). Furthermore, this substorm-driven precipitation displays a pronounced dawn-dusk asymmetry, likely due to the preferential distribution of chorus waves. These results establish substorms as a critical, independent driver of the supply and loss of electrons below ∼100 keV, advancing our understanding of radiation belt dynamics across geomagnetic disturbances.

title: Jupiter’s X-ray emissions and prospects for soft X-ray imaging
abstract: X-ray observations of the Jovian system have greatly advanced our understanding of giant-planet magnetospheres and their coupling to moons, plasma sources, and the solar wind. Over four decades of measurements have revealed diverse X-ray emissions originating from Jupiter’s aurorae, disk, the Io plasma torus, the surfaces of its moons, and the radiation belt. Among these, the aurora remains the most luminous source, with soft X-rays produced primarily by charge exchange between highly charged heavy ions and Jupiter’s upper atmosphere, and hard X-rays generated through electron bremsstrahlung. Recent discoveries, including quasi-periodic pulsations, dawn-storm-related enhancements, and hemispheric asymmetries, highlight the complex interplay among internal magnetospheric processes, Io-driven mass loading, and variable solar wind conditions. Meanwhile, rapid developments in soft X-ray imaging technologies, particularly wide-field lobster-eye optics and radiation-tolerant CMOS detectors, offer new opportunities for global, time-resolved studies of Jupiter’s magnetosphere based on close-range imaging missions. Such instruments could, for the first time, capture continuous X-ray images of the auroral regions, the Io plasma torus, and Galilean moons, enabling major progress on long-standing questions concerning particle acceleration, plasma transport, and moon-magnetosphere interactions. This review synthesizes the current understanding of Jovian X-ray emissions, highlights key open problems, and outlines the scientific potential of future soft X-ray planetary missions.

title: Modeling electron fluxes in Earth’s outer radiation belt using fused RBSP and Arase observations
abstract: Relativistic electrons in Earth’s outer radiation belt pose severe hazards to spacecraft, especially during geomagnetic storms when electron fluxes surge. NASA’s Van Allen Probes (RBSP, 2012–2019) provided high quality measurements but did not span a full solar cycle, whereas JAXA’s ongoing Arase mission extends in situ observations into the subsequent cycle. Quantitative data fusion across missions is hampered by differences in instrument response and energy coverage. Here we developed a neural network based cross calibration framework to harmonize electron flux measurements from the Extremely High Energy Electron Experiment on board Arase and the Magnetic Electron Ion Spectrometer on board RBSP. The framework generates abundant synthetic coincidence samples to compensate for the scarcity of true conjunctions, thereby enabling comprehensive calibration and data merging across missions. Using the fused data set, we trained a nowcasting model that predicts outer belt electron fluxes two hours ahead from solar wind parameters and geomagnetic indices. The results show that extending the temporal coverage of the training set markedly improves prediction accuracy by increasing the number and diversity of storm time events included in the training data. These findings highlight the critical role of cross satellite calibration and long term observations in advancing space weather nowcasting, deepening our understanding of radiation belt dynamics, and improving orbit risk assessment.

title: Spatiotemporal variation of near-surface oxygen concentration on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau based on an experimental observation network of georeferenced oxygen sensors
abstract: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is a key regulator of regional and global climate, yet limited observational data have constrained understanding of its near-surface atmospheric oxygen dynamics. To address this gap, a ground-based experimental georeferenced observation network (2022–2024) was established to obtain high-resolution measurements of near-surface relative oxygen concentration (ROC) and its environmental drivers. In this study, oxygen values measured by the TD600S electrochemical sensor are interpreted as sensor-measured near-surface oxygen concentrations related to geographical locations and environments, rather than high-precision determinations of dry-air atmospheric oxygen mole fraction. By incorporating humidity and wind speed into a gradient boosting decision tree model, the explained variance of ROC was increased from 82.0% to 93.7%. The contributing factors of ROC, ranked from greatest to smallest influence, were altitude (−45.6%), air temperature (33.2%), vegetation (12.4%), relative humidity (4.9%), and wind speed (−3.9%). Altitude and air temperature exhibited linear relationships with ROC while wind speed, humidity, and leaf area index exhibited nonlinear relationships. ROC increases from winter to summer, peaking in July, with turning points occurring in March and September. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of the seasonal and monthly variability of ROC on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, providing valuable implications for evaluating hypoxia-related eco-environmental and health risks.

title: Amorphous calcium carbonate decomposition and implications for subduction-zone carbon cycle
abstract: Calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) plays a central role in the deep carbon cycle, yet its stability under varying oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) in the mantle wedge remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigated the stability of amorphous CaCO 3 in redox-buffered systems at 0.5–3.0 GPa and 900–1180 °C. Our results reveal that its phase stability and quenched morphology are highly f O 2 -dependent. Under oxidizing conditions (>ΔFMQ−1), amorphous CaCO 3 remains chemically stable and quenches to coarse calcite (>100 µm). Conversely, reducing conditions at approximately ΔFMQ−2 or below promotes partial decomposition of CaCO 3 and the formation of nanoscale graphite, together with finer-grained aragonite (30–60 µm). These results suggest that localized and transient redox heterogeneities in the mantle wedge may destabilize subducted carbonates. The formation of graphite provides constraints on redox-dependent carbonate destabilization and elemental-carbon sequestration in subduction zones.

title: Driving mechanism for spatiotemporal heterogeneity O3 formation sensitivity by VOCR-FNR interaction
abstract: Ozone (O 3 ) pollution has emerged as a significant challenge for regional air quality management. Understanding the impact of anthropogenic emission variations on ozone formation sensitivity (OFS) is crucial. This study systematically analyzes the spatiotemporal distribution and vertical structural evolution of OFS over Tianjin from 2019 to 2024 by synergistically applying the near-surface volatile organic compound reactivity (VOCR) isopleth method and the tropospheric column ratio of formaldehyde to nitrogen dioxide (HCHO/NO 2 , FNR). The analysis integrates ground-based O 3 -NO x data from Tianjin’s ambient air quality monitoring network and Sentinel-5P satellite retrievals of HCHO/NO 2 column concentrations. The results indicate that the observed reduction in O 3 pollution in 2021 was primarily driven by two factors: an overall decline in VOC emissions and an earlier daily peak in nitrogen oxides (NO x ) concentrations. This combination enhanced O 3 depletion by NO. Further analysis clarified that OFS over Tianjin generally operated within a VOC-limited regime. The FNR exhibited distinct spatiotemporal heterogeneity: seasonally, values were lower in winter and higher in summer; spatially, values were lower in urban centers and higher in suburban areas. and demonstrated complex vertical variation. There was no significant difference in the FNR value between the lower layer and the troposphere layer during the ozone season. Notably, reduced emissions of anthropogenic VOCs were identified as a key factor lowering FNR in the upper troposphere. This work confirms that combining near-surface and tropospheric observations can effectively resolve vertical differences in OFS. In the future, O 3 pollution control efforts should coordinate reductions in both VOCs and NO x emissions. In particular, VOC emissions should be prioritized for reduction in spring and autumn, while NO x emissions should be the focus of mitigation in summer.

title: A new method of inverting crustal strain rates based on micro-block modeling and its application to southern California
abstract: Crustal strain rate is an important indicator for seismic hazard assessment. However, many existing inversion methods either have limited capability to model the first-order crustal motion associated with block rotation and translation or incorporate unreasonable spatial interpolation, therefore reducing the magnitude of the estimated strain rates and the effective spatial resolution of observations. Here, we develop a novel method for inverting crustal strain rates inspired by the microplate model. A deforming region is discretized into micro-blocks based on the spatial locations of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) stations. The motion and strain rates of each micro-block are estimated based on horizontal GNSS velocities and the constraints that adjacent blocks have equal motion velocities on their common boundaries. To validate the method, we perform both synthetic experiments and an application to southern California, and compare the results with those derived from other neighborhood methods. The experiments show that our method provides a data-adaptive representation of strain rate patterns that captures more detailed localized variations while suppressing spurious anomalies, demonstrating strong robustness. In addition, our results identify three localized regions in the Ventura Basin, the Los Angeles basin, and the southern Eastern California Shear Zone, with the median values of the second invariant strain rates exceeding 250 nanostrain/a. Moreover, our method can quantify the relative contributions of two pairs of approximately parallel fault branches, the San Jacinto Fault—the Coachella segment of the San Andreas Fault (CoSAF), and the Santa Cruz Mountains segment of the San Andreas Fault (ScSAF)—the Calaveras Fault, to crustal strain accumulation. The seismic hazards within these three localized areas and along the CoSAF and ScSAF warrant particular attention.

title: Changes in ice-ocean stress and ice-ocean mechanical energy flux associated with Antarctic sea ice regime shift
abstract: Changes in ice-ocean stress and ice-ocean mechanical energy flux associated with the regime shift in Antarctic sea ice extent (SIE) are investigated for the first time using daily satellite-derived sea ice records and simulated ocean surface currents. During the SIE retreat phase, positive zonal ice-ocean stress is substantially enhanced, increasing by 33% relative to the expanded SIE condition, whereas negative zonal and meridional ice-ocean stresses decrease by 20% and 33%, respectively. Vertical motion is also intensified, with pronounced upwelling and downwelling anomalies in the Ross Sea, central Weddell Sea, and the 90°–135°E sector. Overall, the ice-ocean mechanical energy flux acts primarily as an energy sink, dissipating ocean kinetic energy, although positive energy input appears in the Weddell Sea and Ross Sea. The total energy dissipation associated with ice-ocean stress reaches 31.97 GW, of which 5.94 and 26.04 GW are attributable to the time-mean and time-varying components of ice-ocean stress acting on the corresponding ocean surface currents, respectively. During the transition to the retreat phase, energy loss through ice-ocean stress strengthens markedly, particularly in the Ross Sea and the 90°–180°E sector; however, the concurrent intensification of both mechanical energy input and dissipation results in nonsignificant net changes in the circumpolar integral. Crucially, a weak correlation between wind speed and ice-ocean stress reveals that the rapid sea ice decline has diminished internal ice stress, forcing the ice-ocean stress to more directly balance wind stress. These findings highlight the important role of Antarctic SIE variability in altering momentum transfer efficiency, profoundly impacting the upper-ocean momentum budget and, more broadly, the ocean general circulation within the coupled air-ice-ocean system.

title: Passive continental margin rifting: A key driver of Late Paleozoic tectonic-environmental events
abstract: The Permian was a critical interval in Earth’s history, marked by a series of major global tectonic and environmental events. Among these, the passive continental margin rifting along the northern margin of Gondwana is one of the most important tectonic events, yet its spatiotemporal evolution, mechanisms, and environmental consequences remain poorly understood. Here we present new zircon U-Pb age, geochemical data, and Sr-Nd-Hf isotopic compositions for granitic porphyry (282 Ma), gabbro (266 Ma), and dacite (263 Ma) from the South Qiangtang Terrane. Combined with Permian magmatic and sedimentary records from South Qiangtang, Baoshan, Himalayas, Lhasa, northeastern Arabian margin and Central Iran Terranes, these data allow us to reconstruct the spatiotemporal evolution, geodynamic processes, and environmental impacts of this rifting. Our main findings include: (1) Permian passive continental margin rifting occurred widely along the northern margins of African Gondwana, Indian Gondwana, and Australian Gondwana. The northern margin of Indian Gondwana was the rift center, where rifting was most intense, facilitating the opening of the Meso-Tethys Ocean during the Kungurian. (2) The Early Permian passive continental margin rifting was induced by slab pull acting on pre-existing weak zones, entering the Middle Permian, the passive continental margin rifting was primarily driven by sediment loading. (3) Permian passive continental margin rifting facilitated the termination of the Late Paleozoic Ice Age and the flourishing of the global Permian Chert Event. This study shows that Late Paleozoic passive continental margin rifting not only generated large-scale magmatism but also profoundly influenced global climate, ocean chemistry, and biological evolution through deep-surface coupling.

title: Enrichment mechanism of Nb in the Bayan Obo REE-Nb-Fe deposit, North China: Insights from pyrochlore group minerals
abstract: The world-class Bayan Obo REE-Nb-Fe deposit in North China is the world’s major source of rare earth elements (REEs) and second largest niobium (Nb). Although REE mineralization in this deposit has been extensively investigated, the mechanisms responsible for Nb enrichment remain poorly constrained. In this study, we examine hydrothermally altered pyrochlore with patchy zoning and identify two chemically and texturally distinct generations: an earlier pyrochlore (Pcl-a) enriched in Si, Al, F, C, Na, Sr, Fe, Th, and U, and a later pyrochlore (Pcl-b) enriched in Nb, Ti, Ca, Ba, and REEs. Nanoscale veinlets within Pcl-b contain inclusions of bastnäsite, parisite, ilmenite, and magnetite. Pcl-b formed via fluid-induced coupled dissolution-reprecipitation of Pcl-a, driven by cation-anion substitutions, including Na + +F − ↔□ A +□ Y ; Si 4+ +Al 3+ ↔Nb 5+ +Ti 2+ ; Sr 2+ +Fe 2+ +Pb 2+ +U 4+ +Th 4+ -2Ca 2+ +2Ba 2+ +2REE 3+ . Based on these observations, we propose an evolutionary process of Nb enrichment in which F-rich alkaline hydrothermal fluids promoted extensive precipitation of fluorite and aegirine and facilitated crystallization of hydrothermal pyrochlore (Pcl-a), together with magnetite, ilmenite, and REE minerals. Subsequent fluid-mediated remobilization of REEs, Nb, Fe, and Ti triggered replacement of Pcl-a with Nb-richer Pcl-b and synchronous precipitation of nanoscale mineral inclusions. Results presented here highlight fluid-mediated dissolution-reprecipitation as an important mechanism for localized Nb enrichment in hydrothermal systems.

title: South China Sea warming enhances summer monsoon intraseasonal oscillation
abstract: Intraseasonal oscillations (ISOs) are a dominant mode of natural variability during the South China Sea (SCS) summer monsoon (SCSSM) and play a crucial role in modulating extreme events, such as droughts and floods. Therefore, studying the long-term changes in ISOs during the SCSSM is essential for understanding regional rainfall variability and extremes. Based on the observational and reanalysis datasets from 1980 to 2019, this study identifies a significant increasing trend in ISOs over the central SCS, accompanied by a rise in its contribution to total monsoon variability at a rate of ∼3% decade −1 . A corresponding increase in the intraseasonal moisture variability is also observed, consistent with the key role of moisture in maintaining ISO deep convection. The intraseasonal moisture budget analysis demonstrates that vertical moisture advection is the primary dynamic process responsible for the intraseasonal moistening in the core region, in particular the advection of background moisture by intraseasonal vertical motion. In addition, this advection enhancement is largely attributable to a steepened background moisture gradient, which results from the increased low-level moisture. Moreover, the low-level moisture enhancement is driven by the enhanced surface latent heat flux, ultimately linked to oceanic warming in the central SCS. These findings present the multi-timescale air-sea interactions, whereby the oceanic thermal forcing modifies ISOs during the SCSSM. These results provide insights for understanding the regional climate responses to ocean warming, and for improving monsoon predictions and projections as well as early warnings of extreme events.

title: Decadal modulation of the North Pacific SST seasonal cycle by summer mixed layer depth variability
abstract: The seasonal cycle is the dominant component of Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability in the North Pacific, with substantial climatic and ecological implications. While previous studies have focused on its long-term intensification under anthropogenic forcing, this study reveals pronounced decadal variability in the amplitude of the SST seasonal cycle during 1958–2024. The amplitude increases before the 1970s and after the 2000s, but decreases during the intervening decades, with a peak-to-trough range of 6.1% relative to the climatological seasonal cycle. Regression patterns show that this variability is the strongest in the central and eastern North Pacific, extending to approximately 25 m depth. Mixed layer heat budget analyses using multiple ocean datasets identify Mixed Layer Depth (MLD) variability as the primary driver. A simplified reconstruction model further reveals that summer MLD variations dominate the low-frequency variability, while winter MLD plays a minimal role. This asymmetry arises because SST is more sensitive to summer MLD changes due to its shallower climatological depth, an assumption central to our modeling framework. Moreover, the summer MLD variability is modulated by wind stress forcing associated with the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). In particular, persistent enhancement of surface winds during the positive phase of PDO deepens the summer MLD and reduces the SST seasonal amplitude during the 1970s and 2000s, whereas weakened winds during negative PDO phases lead to shallower MLD and enhanced amplitude before the 1970s and after the 2000s. These findings advance our understanding of North Pacific climate variability and benefit efforts to predict the climate on a decadal scale.

title: ArchLips: A novel tool to break the bottleneck in archaeal lipidomics research
Discovery and significance of Late Cretaceous anoxic events in the West African Rift System
abstract: As a major focus of Earth science research, the Cretaceous Oceanic Anoxic Events (OAEs) provide valuable geological archives for understanding interactions among the Earth’s atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and lithosphere during this period. The low-latitude West African Rift System (WARS) preserves a relatively complete Cretaceous stratigraphic succession; however, studies of anoxic events within this region remain limited, leaving a critical gap in global records. This study focuses on the Upper Cretaceous shale succession in the Termit Basin of the WARS. By integrating multi-proxy records of changes in paleoclimate and paleoenvironment, including organic carbon isotopes, the Chemical Index of Alteration (CIA), iron speciation, and phosphorus phase partitioning, four intervals were identified (Intervals I–IV from bottom to top). The following main insights were obtained: (1) the Upper Cretaceous shale succession in the Termit Basin provides an excellent record of the Late Cretaceous oceanic anoxic and climatic events, among which Interval I corresponds to OAE2, Interval II to the post-OAE2 global cooling event, and Interval III to OAE3; (2) Interval I was deposited under oxic to dysoxic bottom-water conditions, whereas Intervals II–IV were generally deposited under ferruginous anoxic conditions, with only part of Interval II exhibiting ferruginous to weakly euxinic conditions. Although these intervals are similar to OAE2 and OAE3, which were driven by global events such as enhanced continental weathering due to the extreme greenhouse climate and Large Igneous Province (LIP) eruptions, they were more strongly controlled by regional processes, including sedimentary phosphorus recycling and local magmatic activity; (3) Upper Cretaceous source-rock in this basin was mainly controlled by nutrient delivery (especially phosphorus) through multiple pathways, including riverine input, regional magmatic/hydrothermal supply, and recycling from sediments. This study provides new insights into the response mechanisms of Cretaceous OAEs in low-latitude regions, and clarifies the controls on source-rock development in West Africa. Therefore, these findings are scientifically significant for deciphering Cretaceous climatic and environmental evolution, as well as guiding the exploration and development of conventional and unconventional hydrocarbon resources in the region.

title: Solar activity regulates geographical swings of droughts in the circum-North Pacific region with an 11-year cycle
abstract: Drought risk has increased in many regions under ongoing climate change, but changes in the geographical distribution of droughts and their underlying drivers remain poorly understood. Our analysis of summer droughts across the circum-North Pacific regions of Asia and North America (1950–2021) reveals a prominent ∼11-yr cycle of drought region swings with significant covariability between the two continents. We find that solar forcing is associated with the drought swings, with its effects likely amplified by ocean-atmosphere interactions over the Pacific. Tree-ring reconstructions support the existence of a long-term link between drought swings and solar activity spanning at least 700 yr. Our findings highlight a pronounced trend of shifting drought patterns over the past century, portending heightened risk of severe drought in the southwestern US, Mexico, and North China. Understanding these spatial shifts provides new insights for drought forecasting and prevention strategies.

title: High-resolution reconstruction of the 1973 MS7.6 Luhuo earthquake rupture from historical aerial imagery: Insights into fault behavior and seismic-aseismic coupling
abstract: High-resolution mapping and dense displacement measurements of coseismic surface ruptures are fundamental for understanding rupture dynamics, fault segmentation, and faulting behavior. However, many significant historical earthquakes still lack detailed spatial characterization due to the scarcity of high-resolution historical imagery. The destructive 1973 M S 7.6 Luhuo earthquake on the Eastern Tibetan Plateau, produced a ∼90-km-long surface rupture along the Xianshuihe fault system, whose southeastern termination has since exhibited persistent aseismic creep. Because traditional field surveys failed to capture spatially continuous datasets of rupture geometry and coseismic displacement, the primary structural controls on rupture propagation and its mechanical coupling with fault creep remain poorly constrained. Here, we integrate an archive dataset of high-resolution historical aerial photographs acquired shortly after the 1973 event with targeted field investigations to reconstruct the surface rupture trace and coseismic slip distribution along a ∼70-km-long central segment flanking the epicenter at unprecedented resolution. Our mapping reveals a predominantly narrow and continuous main rupture zone, except near the epicenter where the deformation zone widens to ∼140 m and splits into at least two strands. The surface rupture is dominated by NW-striking en-echelon cracks, complemented by secondary NW and EW striking conjugate structures. High-density displacement measurements yield a maximum left-lateral coseismic horizontal offset of ∼4 m in the central segment, with slip decreasing asymmetrically toward the rupture terminations. The high-resolution constraints demonstrate that the first-order coseismic slip distribution is controlled by geometric complexities, whereas along-strike lithological variation exerts a secondary influence by modulating localized deformation styles. Furthermore, a pronounced spatial anti-correlation between the 1973 coseismic slip and present-day creep rates along the Luhuo fault reveals a direct mechanical link between dynamic rupture propagation, shallow aseismic strain release, and long-term fault behavior. These findings provide critical insights into slip budgets and strain partitioning along major intracontinental strike-slip fault systems.

title: Field-Aligned currents in eastward and westward auroral structures
abstract: Auroral substorms play a fundamental role in magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling and nightside magnetic reconnection. Although field-aligned currents (FACs) and the evolution of westward traveling surges (WTS) during substorms have been extensively studied, the FAC characteristics associated with eastward-expanding auroral surges (EEAS) remain poorly understood. Using conjugate observations from the Poker Flat Incoherent Scatter Radar (PFISR), all-sky imagers (PFASI) and Swarm satellites, we investigated the complete evolution of EEAS during the substorm recovery phase and compared the characteristics of EEAS with those of a typical WTS. Our analysis reveals that during the substorm recovery phase, rapid interplanetary magnetic field (IMF) fluctuations influence the evolution of EEAS, which are accompanied by strong convection shears and structured, multipolar FAC systems. We find that both EEAS and WTS are triggered by low-density, equatorward plasma flows originating from the polar cap boundary. However, these phenomena differ fundamentally in their propagation directions and associated FAC configurations, suggesting distinct underlying physical mechanisms.

title: Leaf wax distribution and carbon isotope composition as credible indicators of past typical C4 grasses on the Chinese Loess Plateau
abstract: Over the past decades, extensive efforts have been devoted to investigating the expansion history of global C 4 plants and its climatic implications. However, the lack of taxonomic information on plant species has impeded the clear identification of climatic drivers underlying the expansion of C 4 plants as reconstructed via stable carbon isotope analysis. Here we show that the distribution of leaf wax n -alkanes for a dominant C 4 plant species ( Bothriochloa ischaemum ) differs markedly from that for other species of plants in China. Characterized by relatively higher ratio of n -alkanes with 33 carbon atoms (C 33 ) to C 29 or C 31 homologues, the contribution of Bothriochloa ischaemum can result in more positive carbon isotope values for sedimentary C 33 compared with C 29 and C 31 . We further propose that the combined application of distributions and compound-specific carbon isotope patterns of leaf wax n -alkanes in geological archives allows for the reconstruction of variations in species of C 4 plants, and the associated paleoclimatic contexts can be inferred according to the modern habitat of these plants. By applying this integrated approach, we can delineate the potential shifts in plant species and their driving mechanisms over the past 800,000 yr on the Chinese Loess Plateau, thereby resolving the long-standing controversy regarding the climatic implications of Quaternary C 4 plant evolution in this region.

title: Anthropogenic CO2-induced seawater acidification suppressed dimethylsulfide emissions in the northwestern Pacific marginal seas
abstract: Marine dimethylsulfide (DMS) emissions exert a pivotal control on climate regulation via aerosol formation. Nevertheless, the biogeochemical cycle of DMS under seawater acidification remains poorly understood. Here we present integrated biogeochemical analyses that combine field observations, historical datasets, process-based modeling, and ship-based incubation experiments to elucidate pH-dependent regulatory mechanisms governing the cycling of DMS and its precursor dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) across the northwestern Pacific marginal seas. Our findings identify pH as the key driver of DMS spatial variability; moreover, DMS removal processes are highly sensitive to pH. Structural equation modeling reveals pH-driven cascading impacts on DMS mediated by dinoflagellate biomass. Incubation experiments further demonstrate that decreasing pH reduces high DMSP-producer abundance and suppresses both DMS biological production and removal rates, collectively inhibiting net DMS accumulation. These findings indicate that seawater acidification under the high-emission SSP5-8.5 scenario will reduce global marginal seas DMS emissions by 35%–66% by 2100, which may intensity regional and global warming. Our research provides new insights into the feedback mechanisms linking marine sulfur biogeochemical cycles and global climate change.

title: Extreme 2023–2024 Indian Ocean Basin warming triggered by oceanic heat redistribution
abstract: In 2023–2024, an exceptionally strong Indian Ocean Basin (IOB) warming event occurred following an extreme positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and coincided with a strong El Niño. A unique feature of this event was the unprecedented and widespread warming in the eastern tropical Indian Ocean (ETIO) during boreal winter (DJF). Unlike previous IOB events (e.g., 1997–1998, 2015–2016, and 2019–2020), where anomalous air-sea heat exchange played a crucial role, the 2023–2024 ETIO warming was primarily driven by oceanic processes. We find that nonlinear zonal and vertical advections played a leading role in triggering the ETIO warming in December, with meridional advection sustaining and broadening the warming through February. This oceanic response reflects distinct dynamical changes in the Walker circulation associated with the co-occurrence of strong positive IOD and El Niño events. Our results highlight the critical role of anomalous atmospheric circulation in modulating oceanic heat redistribution, ultimately triggering the extreme 2023–2024 IOB warming.

title: Challenges and advances in soil tetraether-lipid-based temperature reconstruction in global arid and semi-arid regions: Insights from the Pan-Third Pole
abstract: The Holocene is a critical interval for understanding natural climate variability and testing climate mechanisms relevant to future warming. However, reliable terrestrial temperature proxies remain a major bottleneck in palaeoclimate reconstruction. Soil microbial glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGTs) have become important palaeotemperature indicators, but the conventional brGDGT-based MBT’ 5ME index often produces biased estimates in arid and semi-arid regions. Recent studies have addressed this limitation by optimizing brGDGT calibrations through data-driven approaches and extending the marine TEX 86 proxy to soil systems. Focusing on the Pan-Third Pole region, this review synthesizes recent progress and common challenges in soil GDGT-based temperature reconstruction, and evaluates its application to Holocene loess-palaeosol records. Overall, the field is shifting from single empirical indices toward a dual-proxy framework that combines complementary GDGT indicators, improving the potential for reconstructing temperature in complex terrestrial settings. However, major uncertainties remain regarding the climatic meaning of GDGT signals, including their seasonal versus annual and air versus soil temperature sensitivities, the influence of non-thermal factors, and the applicability limits of different proxies. These uncertainties hinder comparisons among GDGT records and between proxy reconstructions and climate model simulations. Future work should strengthen coordinated observations of air and soil temperatures alongside GDGT distributions, advance the integrated analysis of microbial communities, key environmental factors, and lipid molecular responses, and incorporate palaeoclimate data assimilation to impose stronger mechanistic constraints on terrestrial GDGT-based temperature reconstructions. In particular, the temperature response of soil TEX 86 should be continuously evaluated across broader spatial scales and environmental gradients, thereby providing more robust terrestrial evidence for understanding the record-model discrepancy underlying the Holocene temperature conundrum.

title: Advances in multiscale gas-water two-phase flow mechanisms during deep coalbed methane development
abstract: Deep coalbed methane (CBM) development represents an important technological pathway for advancing China’s unconventional natural gas reserves and production while supporting the coordinated achievement of the “dual carbon” goals. Constrained by complex deep geological conditions, deep CBM wells commonly exhibit rapid production decline, substantial interwell productivity variability, and a high proportion of low-efficiency wells. Focusing on the multiscale gas-water two-phase flow mechanisms during deep CBM development, this paper systematically reviews recent domestic and international research progress in terms of reservoir conditions and depth effects, gas-water occurrence and transformation mechanisms, permeability evolution and multiphase multiscale flow mechanisms, and experimental characterization and numerical simulation methods. The synthesis indicates that deep coal seams are generally subjected to a “three-high” environment characterized by high temperature, high reservoir pressure, and high in situ stress. Depth-dependent effects continuously constrain multiscale gas-water flow processes by modifying coal-rock mechanical properties, pore-fracture structures, reservoir connectivity, and engineering stimulation responses. With increasing burial depth, CBM occurrence progressively evolves from an adsorption-dominated state to the coexistence of adsorbed and free gas, while the gas-water occurrence pattern and its dynamic evolution affect fluid mobility and continuous gas supply capacity. The dynamic conversion between adsorbed and free gas, together with diffusion-seepage coupling, is an important factor influencing the establishment of gas-flow pathways and production capacity. Permeability evolution in deep coal reservoirs is closely related to adsorption/desorption, effective stress, and the dynamic evolution of pore-fracture networks. Overall, multiscale gas-water two-phase flow in deep coal reservoirs is a continuous process involving the occurrence, transformation, diffusion, and seepage of multiphase fluids within hierarchical pore-fracture networks, and is jointly regulated by pore structure, gas-water occurrence characteristics, coal structural heterogeneity, and multifield coupling. This paper distills the major understandings in this field and identifies key issues and future research directions. These synthesized insights can provide theoretical support and a scientific basis for deepening research on multiscale gas-water two-phase flow mechanisms in deep CBM reservoirs and supporting efficient deep CBM development.

title: Understanding the interdecadal change in the tropical Asian summer monsoon onset timing: A perspective from the basin-scale shifting of Indo-Pacific warming pattern
abstract: The onset timing of tropical Asian summer monsoon (TASM) was observed to have experienced two pronounced interdecadal shifts during 1979–2024. Specifically, remarkable advancement of the monsoon onset occurred around the late 1990s, while significant delay appeared at the beginning of the 2010s. In this study, the two interdecadal shifts are proposed to be influenced by different warming patterns of sea surface temperature (SST) in the Indo-Pacific Ocean. For the advanced onset of the TASM after 1998, an intensified La Niña-like SST warming pattern in the Pacific played a crucial role. The corresponding positive SST anomalies in the western North Pacific enhanced atmospheric convective heating, which consequently induced an anomalous lower-level cyclonic circulation in the TASM region through a westward Rossby wave response. Meanwhile, the La Niña-like SST pattern can strengthen the Walker circulation, further intensifying convection over the western North Pacific and the aforesaid Rossby wave response, and then advancing the TASM onset. However, since the beginning of the 2010s, the Pacific La Niña-like SST warming pattern has weakened, accompanied by a rapid warming in the tropical Indian Ocean (TIO). The TIO warming exerted a growing negative influence on the TASM onset by strengthening local convection that forced an eastward atmospheric Kelvin wave. The associated tropical lower-level easterly anomalies postponed the monsoon onset. The above diagnostic results are well verified by numerical simulations. Our findings underscore the significant contribution of different Indo-Pacific SST warming patterns to the two interdecadal shifts of the TASM onset timing in recent decades.

title: Crystallinity-dependent Lewis acidity regulates phosphate adsorption on iron minerals
abstract: Iron minerals are ubiquitous in Earth’s surface waters and soils, serving as effective adsorbents for phosphorus (P) removal. However, the underlying mechanism linking P removal efficiency to the crystallinity and Lewis acidity of iron minerals remains unclear under varying hydrogeochemical conditions. Therefore, this study reveals the intrinsic relationship between crystallinity and Lewis acidity for ferrihydrite{110}, goethite{110}, and hematite {001}, as well as their impact on P adsorption. Mechanisms insights were obtained using X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results demonstrate that reduced crystallinity correlates with enhanced Lewis acidity. This crystallinity-dependent Lewis acidity originates from Fe-O orbital coupling: high crystallinity strengthens Fe-O orbital coupling, whereas low crystallinity weakens this process, resulting in more unsaturated Fe sites with available empty orbitals. Consequently, differences in Lewis acidity directly govern P adsorption efficiency, with the adsorption capacities following the order: ferrihydrite>goethite>hematite. These findings suggest that the effect of iron mineral crystallinity on Lewis acidity should not be overlooked, which has important implications for P cycling in soil and water ecosystems.

title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vertical velocities in the tropical western Pacific Ocean from moored velocity measurements
abstract: Vertical flow in the tropical Pacific Ocean plays a crucial role in vertical exchange of oceanic heat and mass, biogeochemical cycling, and climate change. However, due to observational limitations, the spatiotemporal characteristics of vertical velocity in this region remain poorly understood. Here we present vertical velocity estimates from continuous velocity measurements from Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs), which were mounted on a triangular array of four subsurface moorings in the North Equatorial Countercurrent (NECC) region centered near 4.7°N, 142°E and sustained for 40 months from December 2017 to March 2021. The vertical velocity was calculated from the continuity equation using the horizontal velocity components measured by the ADCPs. Upwelling was observed in the mean vertical velocity at and above the NECC core, peaking at 1.2×10 −5 m s −1 at 70 m, in contrast to the basin-averaged near-surface downwelling typical for this latitude. Below 110 m, the flow transitioned to downwelling, with a peak velocity of −2.5×10 −5 m s −1 observed near 240 m. Significant fluctuations in vertical velocity were observed, with alternating upwelling and downwelling episodes driven primarily by zonal divergence and convergence associated with NECC acceleration and deceleration. The dominant seasonal variability of the vertical velocity was linked to fluctuations in the depth of the 20 °C isotherm driven by remotely forced Rossby waves, whereas interannual variability was governed by local wind stress curl through Ekman pumping. Vertical velocity substantially modulated subsurface water properties, driving fluctuations in potential temperature and density—manifested as isotherm shoaling during upwelling and deepening during downwelling. In contrast, near-surface temperature was considerably less affected. Intense vertical motion was spatially confined to the 3°–6°N latitude band, with no concurrent signals at adjacent latitudes, suggesting a mechanism distinct from equatorial upwelling systems.

title: Cretaceous plate reorganization in the western Pacific: Deep-mantle mechanisms and surface feedbacks
abstract: The Cretaceous represents a pivotal interval of global tectonic reorganization. During this period, plate evolution in the western Pacific profoundly influenced mantle dynamics and the thermal-mechanical structure of the lithosphere along the East Asian continental margin, exerting significant impacts on surface landscape development and climate. Integrating geological, geophysical, and geochemical evidence, this study systematically investigates the Cretaceous plate evolution in the western Pacific and explores the potential coupling between deep-mantle dynamics and surface systems. The results indicate that a mid-Cretaceous episode of intense subduction, characterized by a “slab-superflux” influx of the paleo-Pacific (Izanagi) Plate, may have enhanced deep-surface coupling. This event likely perturbed the stability of the Pacific large low-shear-velocity province (LLSVP) boundary, facilitating superplume upwelling and contributing to the formation of large igneous provinces (LIPs) in the western Pacific. Concurrently, strengthened asthenospheric return flow toward the East Asian margin promoted lithospheric thinning, rift-basin development, and widespread volcanism. In the climate system, superplume-related LIP eruptions are widely regarded as major drivers of the Cretaceous greenhouse climate and Oceanic Anoxic Events (OAEs). We further suggest that subduction dynamics may have modulated the magnitude and tempo of these climatic perturbations, although additional evidence is needed. Integrating these observations, we propose a conceptual framework linking plate reorganization, mantle convection reconfiguration, lithospheric deformation, and surface feedbacks, offering new insights into deep-Earth controls on surface processes.

title: Crustal structure and lateral growth mechanism of the northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau: Constraints from seismic wide-angle reflection/refraction probing
abstract: To investigate the crustal structure of the northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, particularly its thickening and lateral growth mechanisms, we completed a 1200-km-long seismic wide-angle reflection/refraction profile extending from Nangqên in the Qiangtang block in the south to Yabrai in the Alxa block in the north. Along this profile, abundant and clear seismic records were obtained, and velocity structure models of the crust and uppermost mantle were established for the northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau and its adjacent tectonic units. The results show that the P-wave velocity of the crystalline crust in the northeastern Tibetan Plateau ranges from 5.4 to 6.7 km/s, with an average velocity of 6.10–6.15 km/s, which is 5.1%–5.9% lower than that of the stable cratonic crust surrounding the plateau. The tectonic deformation within the plateau is constrained by multiple factors, including the crustal structural characteristics of adjacent blocks, the mode of regional tectonic stress, and the material and energy exchange between different layers. Along the profile, the crustal thickness varies from 51 to 70 km. Specifically, the crust is ~61 km thick beneath the Lenglongling area on the northern margin of the Qilian Mountains, ~51 km thick beneath the Qinghai Lake-Gonghe Basin on the southern margin of the Qilian Mountains, and up to 70 km thick beneath the fold belt on the eastern side of the Qiangtang block. The crust exhibits a wave-like thickness variation from north to south. In the central segment of the Bayan Har block, the uppermost mantle rises significantly, the Moho discontinuity is disrupted, and mantle-derived materials intrude and fuse with intracrustal media, thereby modifying and reconstructing a high-velocity structure of 6.9 km/s in the lower crust. This demonstrates the diversity of energy and material exchange between the crust and uppermost mantle and the diversity of crustal tectonic evolution. The Alxa block has undergone crustal thickening; the Hexi Corridor on its southern margin exhibits a strong northward tilt of the crust and reduced seismic velocities, revealing the outward extension of plateau tectonic stress and the corresponding tectonic response of the peripheral crust, indicating a trend toward “plateauization”. Combined with GPS, regional seismic, geological, and other geophysical findings, the dynamic evolution process of crustal thickening and lateral growth in the northeastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau is further discussed.

title: Proxy-specific spectral signatures: Implications for reconstructing full-spectrum climate variability
Particle simulations of solar wind sputtering and scattering at asteroid 2016 HO3
abstract: Asteroid 2016 HO 3 (Kamo’oalewa) is one of Earth’s quasi-satellites and the target of China’s Tianwen-2 mission. This study investigates the plasma environment and resultant particle emissions from 2016 HO 3 by combining three-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations with a test-particle method. The PIC simulations reveal that the asteroid’s surface charges to potentials of up to +12 V on the sunlit side and down to −30 V on the nightside. Using this potential structure and energy and angular distributions of scattering and sputtering taken from lunar energetic neutral atom observations (not validated descriptions of the asteroid), we employ test-particle simulations to predict the fluxes of scattered solar wind protons and sputtered ions at the Tianwen-2 mission’s planned science orbit. The proton scattering rate is assumed to be 0.4% based on lunar data. Under typical solar wind conditions, we quantitatively determine the fluxes from both processes. At a distance of 300 m from the asteroid, the peak flux of scattered protons near the subsolar point is on the order of 10 3 cm −2 s −1 . With a sputter yield of 10 −4 for silicon ions (Si + ), the peak flux is about 10 2 cm −2 s −1 when combining inc, ident hydrogen and helium ions. We further show that the fluxes of scattering and sputtering increase with the enhanced solar wind density or velocity. The energy spectrum of sputtered ions is more sensitive to changes in sheath potential than that of scattered protons. The secondary electron emission due to either incident electrons or photons modifies the sheath potential and slightly enhances the sputtered ion flux. Our results elucidate the plasma environment of asteroid 2016 HO 3 and serve as a critical reference for planning and interpreting in-situ particle measurements for the Tianwen-2 mission.
